title: Matrices and determinants
description: Questions on matrices and their products, determinants as signed areas and volumes, and Cramer's rule.

questions.question: In a matrix, where is the entry $$a_{23}$$?
questions.explanation: The first number is the row (:ref{#matrix-size}).

questions.question: What does transposing a matrix do?
options: Reverses the order of the rows
questions.explanation: Row $$i$$ of $$A^{\mathsf T}$$ is column $$i$$ of $$A$$ (:ref{#transpose}).

questions.question: What is $$\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$$?
questions.explanation: Each entry is a row times the column (:ref{#matrix-times-column}); also the sum of the two columns (:ref{#matrices-column-combination}).

questions.question: Where does $$X \mapsto AX$$ send the unit column $$E^1$$?
questions.explanation: $$AE^j = A^j$$ (:ref{#columns-images}): the columns record where the unit columns go.

questions.question: Is $$AB = BA$$ for all square matrices $$A$$ and $$B$$?
options: Yes, if they are the same size
questions.explanation: Like moves of the plane, doing one then the other depends on the order (:ref{#matrix-product-rules}).

questions.question: What is the area of the parallelogram on $$(3, 1)$$ and $$(1, 2)$$?
questions.explanation: $$\lvert 3 \cdot 2 - 1 \cdot 1 \rvert$$ (:ref{#signed-area}).

questions.question: What does a negative determinant mean for a 2 by 2 matrix?
options: The mapping flips the plane over
questions.explanation: A negative determinant means the turn from the first column to the second is clockwise, so the picture comes out as its mirror image (:ref{#signed-area}).

questions.question: Is $$\det\begin{pmatrix} 2 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$$ zero, and what does that mean?
options: Yes: the columns lie on one line through $$O$$
Yes: the matrix is the identity
questions.explanation: $$4 - 4 = 0$$, and the second column is twice the first, so the parallelogram is flat (:ref{#signed-area}).

questions.question: Swapping the two columns of a matrix does what to its determinant?
questions.explanation: Property D6 (:ref{#det2-properties}): a swap reverses the orientation.

questions.question: For a 2 by 2 matrix, what is $$\det(3A)$$?
questions.explanation: Each of the two columns is scaled by $$3$$, so by D2 twice the factor is $$3^2$$ (:ref{#det2-properties}).

questions.question: If $$\det A = 2$$ and $$\det B = 5$$, what is $$\det(AB)$$?
questions.explanation: Area factors multiply when one mapping follows another (:ref{#det2-product}).

questions.question: When does a 2 by 2 matrix have an inverse?
options: When its entries are whole numbers
questions.explanation: Then $$A^{-1} = \frac{1}{\det A}\begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix}$$ (:ref{#det2-inverse}).

questions.question: What is the determinant of the matrix with rows $$(2, 0, 0)$$, $$(5, 3, 0)$$, $$(1, 7, 4)$$?
questions.explanation: It is triangular, so the determinant is the product of the diagonal (:ref{#det3-triangular}).

questions.question: Which row or column should you expand along to save work?
options: Any one: they all give the same answer, so pick one with zeros
questions.explanation: Every row and column gives the same number with the checkerboard signs (:ref{#det3-any-row}).

questions.question: Does the diagonal shortcut work for 4 by 4 determinants?
options: Yes, if you copy three columns
questions.explanation: It gives the six terms of the 3 by 3 formula and nothing else (:ref{#sarrus}).

questions.question: What is the determinant of the matrix with rows $$(1, 2, 3)$$, $$(4, 5, 6)$$, $$(7, 8, 9)$$?
questions.explanation: Its middle column is the average of the other two, a combination of them (:ref{#det3-zero}).

questions.question: What does $$\lvert \det A \rvert$$ measure for a 3 by 3 matrix?
options: The length of its first column
The volume of the box on its columns
questions.explanation: The determinant is a signed volume (:ref{#signed-volume}).

questions.question: For a 3 by 3 matrix, what is $$\det(-A)$$?
questions.explanation: $$\det(cA) = c^3\det A$$ (:ref{#properties-scale}), and $$(-1)^3 = -1$$.

questions.question: Adding twice the first column to the third does what to the determinant?
questions.explanation: Property D5 (:ref{#det3-properties}), which in pictures slides the layers of a box (:ref{#properties-shear}).

questions.question: Is $$\det(A + B) = \det A + \det B$$?
options: Not in general: with $$A = B = I$$ it is $$8 \ne 2$$
questions.explanation: Determinants multiply over products (:ref{#det3-product}), not over sums.

questions.question: When does Cramer's rule give the solution of $$AX = B$$?
questions.explanation: Then there is exactly one solution, $$x_j = \frac{D_j}{\det A}$$ (:ref{#cramer}).

questions.question: In Cramer's rule, how is the numerator for $$x_2$$ made?
options: Put $$B$$ in place of the second column of $$A$$
Put $$B$$ in place of the second row
questions.explanation: Since $$B = x_1A^1 + x_2A^2 + x_3A^3$$, properties D1, D2 and D4 leave $$x_2\det A$$ (:ref{#cramer}).

questions.question: If $$\det A = 0$$, how many solutions can $$AX = B$$ have?
questions.explanation: Never exactly one (:ref{#cramer-converse}).

questions.question: How is the inverse of a 3 by 3 matrix with $$\det A \ne 0$$ built?
options: $$\frac{1}{\det A}$$ times the transpose of the matrix of cofactors
questions.explanation: A row times its own cofactors gives $$\det A$$, times another row's gives $$0$$ (:ref{#det3-inverse}).

questions.question: If $$A$$ is 2 by 3 and $$B$$ is 3 by 4, what size is $$AB$$?
questions.explanation: Rows of $$A$$ meet columns of $$B$$; the inner sizes must match (:ref{#matrix-product}).

questions.question: How can three equations in three unknowns be written?
questions.explanation: $$A$$ holds the coefficients, $$X$$ the unknowns and $$B$$ the totals (:ref{#matrix-times-column}).

questions.question: What is $$(AB)^{\mathsf T}$$?
questions.explanation: Transposing reverses the order of a product; the matrices guide proves it in an exercise (:ref{#ex-matrices-transpose-product}).

questions.question: What is the inverse of $$\begin{pmatrix} 4 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix}$$?
questions.explanation: The determinant is $$1$$, so swap the diagonal and change the signs of the others (:ref{#det2-inverse}).

questions.question: What does adding a multiple of one column to the other do to the parallelogram?
questions.explanation: That is property D5 (:ref{#det2-properties}): the determinant doesn't change.

questions.question: What is the determinant of a 3 by 3 matrix with a row of zeros?
options: The product of the other rows
questions.explanation: Expand along that row: every term has a factor $$0$$ (:ref{#det3-any-row}).

questions.question: In the checkerboard of signs for a 3 by 3 determinant, what sign goes with the middle entry $$a_{22}$$?
questions.explanation: The sign is $$(-1)^{2 + 2} = +1$$ (:ref{#det3-any-row}).

questions.question: Why is every column rule also a row rule?
options: Rows and columns are the same
questions.explanation: $$\det A^{\mathsf T} = \det A$$ (:ref{#det3-transpose}), and transposing turns rows into columns.

questions.question: Three columns lie in one plane through $$O$$. What is the determinant?
questions.explanation: The box on them is flat and has no volume (:ref{#det3-zero}).

questions.question: A 3 by 3 matrix has $$A^{\mathsf T} = -A$$. What is $$\det A$$?
questions.explanation: $$\det A = \det A^{\mathsf T}$$ (:ref{#det3-transpose}), which is $$\det(-A) = -\det A$$ (:ref{#properties-scale}), so $$\det A = 0$$.

questions.question: Why does putting $$B$$ in place of column $$1$$ give $$x_1 \det A$$?
options: $$B = x_1A^1 + x_2A^2 + x_3A^3$$, and the terms with a repeated column vanish
questions.explanation: Split $$D(B, A^2, A^3)$$ with D1 and D2; the terms with $$A^2$$ or $$A^3$$ twice are $$0$$ by D4 (:ref{#cramer}).

questions.question: Why do computers solve large systems by elimination instead of Cramer's rule?
options: Cramer's rule is wrong for large systems
Cramer's rule needs far more multiplications as the size grows
questions.explanation: Each determinant is expensive, and Cramer's rule needs one more than the number of unknowns (:ref{#cramer}).
